# P-Pass

> P-Pass backs up the photos on your phone to a computer you already own at
> home. No account, no cloud storage, no NAS, no Docker. Open source
> (AGPL-3.0). Photos move encrypted and directly between your phone and your
> computer, and what lands on the computer are the original files in a folder
> you picked.

## What it does

- You install an app on the computer and an app on the phone, and scan a code
  once to pair them.
- On Android, while both are on the same Wi-Fi, new photos from the phone are
  backed up automatically. No manual step, no cable. On iPhone, backups run
  while the app is open; background continuation is up to iOS.
- Photos travel directly between the phone and the computer, end-to-end
  encrypted. They do not pass through a server of ours. When a direct
  connection is not possible, already-encrypted data is handed over by a relay
  that cannot read it and does not keep it.
- What lands on the computer are the original files, uncompressed, in the
  folder you chose: open them straight from that folder.
- Backups are one-way, phone to computer. Deleting a photo on the phone does
  not delete the copy on the computer.
- No account, no cloud storage. How much you can keep is how much free
  space that drive has.

## Boundaries

- Computers: macOS (Apple silicon) and 64-bit Windows. The Windows installer
  is not code-signed, so SmartScreen shows a warning on first install.
- Phones: Android 8.0+ and iPhone on iOS 16+. The iPhone app is distributed
  through a TestFlight public link, not the App Store.
- Backups run on Wi-Fi by default; the mobile-data switch is off by default.
- The computer has to be awake while a backup is running. With the computer
  off, photos stay on the phone and the transfer resumes where it stopped.
- This is not a sync service and not cloud storage. It is one backup target:
  the computer you chose.
